"title": "[Cursor] Sources: first-class references to tickets, PR comments, and transcripts",

"body": "## Problem

The review document names a why, but the reader cannot see where that why comes from. Tickets get a bare list at the document level, PR comments and agent transcripts get nothing. When the skill writes "reviewers asked for a cap on retries", the reader has to trust it or go hunt for the comment themselves.

The current `tickets` field is a special case of a general concept. A ticket, a PR description, a PR comment, a commit message, and an agent transcript are all sources the skill read to write its prose.

## Proposal

### Schema

Replace `tickets` with a document-level `sources` array. Version locking keeps old documents working.

Most kinds stay locators plus a skill-written gist. PR comments are the exception: the skill copies author, body, and line, because the UI has no vendor API to fetch them later.

```ts
type SourceKind = "ticket" | "pr" | "pr-comment" | "commit" | "transcript";

type Source = {
  id: string;
  kind: SourceKind;
  label: string;        // "#24", "alice on PR #32", "Cursor session · Aug 12"
  url?: string;         // absent for transcripts
  title?: string;
  gist?: string;        // one or two sentences, written by the skill
  part?: string;
  // pr-comment only. Copied at skill time. Git-shaped, not GitHub-shaped.
  author?: string;
  body?: string;        // the comment, faithful
  path?: string;
  side?: "old" | "new";
  line?: number;
};
```

`gist` is still interpretation: the skill restates why this source matters. Ticket bodies, PR descriptions, and transcript text stay out of `review.json`. PR comment `body` is copied on purpose. The URL remains the escape hatch for tickets and for opening the comment on the forge.

Transcripts get a gist and no URL. That is the no-leak guarantee, enforced by shape rather than by policy.

A comment with `path` + `side` + `line` is pinned to that line of live git. A comment without a line (PR conversation, not a review comment) stays a source with a quote, not a diff annotation.

Groups get `sources?: string[]` with ids, so a group can name its sources even when the prose does not cite them inline.

### Inline citations

Prose cites a source with standard markdown link syntax and a reserved scheme:

```json
"why": "Reviewers asked for [a cap on retries](source:s2), and [#24](source:s1) tracks the feature."
```

No new syntax. Agents emit markdown links reliably, and the text degrades to readable prose in any renderer. `validate` resolves every `source:` href against `sources` and fails on unknown ids, the same way hunk-ref coverage works. In the UI a stale id renders as plain text and gets flagged, never invented.

Clicking a citation to a line-pinned comment opens the group that holds that hunk, scrolls to the line, and focuses the quote. That is what makes comments first-class. Citations to tickets, transcripts, or unpinned comments keep the hover card.

### UI

Inline citation renders as primary-colored link text with a text-sized kind icon before the first word (icon about 0.8em, kept on the same line as the first word). Hovering shows a card with the kind, label, gist, and the external link. Tried and rejected: superscript icons (illegible at display size) and inline shadcn badges (break the sentence rhythm, read as UI inserted into prose).

Below the What of each group and of the overview, a `SOURCES` row lists all sources for that scope in the existing metadata register (mono label, one-line gist, external-link arrow, no arrow for transcripts). The overview row replaces the current ticket list and keeps the part color dots. No floating panel.

Line-pinned PR comments also render on the live diff, on that line: author, faithful body, link out. Pierre already pins blame onto file lines via `lineAnnotations`; comments should use the same idea on the group diff. Several comments on one line stack. A pointer whose path or line no longer matches live git is flagged like a stale hunk ref. Git wins. The quote is still shown, the pin is marked broken, never replaced.

Show and hide comments on the diffs with a header toggle in the same register as Wrap. Default on when the review has any line-pinned comment. The control is absent when none exist. Keyboard: `c`. Hiding comments does not hide the Sources row or inline citations. Clicking a citation to a pinned comment still opens the line, and shows that quote even if comments are hidden.

Mockups (against the pr32 fixture, gist row and inline marks; comments-on-diff is not in these shots):

![Overview with inline citations and sources row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/matemolnar8/comprehende/assets/sources-mock/mocks/overview-prefix-icon.png)

![Group with inline citations and sources row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/matemolnar8/comprehende/assets/sources-mock/mocks/group-prefix-icon.png)

### Skill

The skill already reads these sources for the why. New work is: assign ids, write labels and gists, emit `sources`, cite inline where the prose leans on a specific source, and for review comments copy author, body, path, side, and line from the forge. Vendor specifics (how to fetch a GitHub review comment vs a Jira ticket) stay at the skill level.

### Out of scope

- Copying ticket bodies, PR descriptions, or transcript text
- Fetching or refreshing source content at serve time
- Any vendor API in the CLI or UI
- Comment threads as a nested tree (flatten or emit one source per comment)

Most kinds stay locators plus a skill-written gist. PR comments are the exception: the skill copies author, body, and line, because the UI has no vendor API to fetch them later.

```ts
type SourceKind = "ticket" | "pr" | "pr-comment" | "commit" | "transcript";

type Source = {
  id: string;
  kind: SourceKind;
  label: string;        // "#24", "alice on PR #32", "Cursor session · Aug 12"
  url?: string;         // absent for transcripts
  title?: string;
  gist?: string;        // one or two sentences, written by the skill
  part?: string;
  // pr-comment only. Copied at skill time. Git-shaped, not GitHub-shaped.
  author?: string;
  body?: string;        // the comment, faithful
  path?: string;
  side?: "old" | "new";
  line?: number;
};
```

`gist` is still interpretation: the skill restates why this source matters. Ticket bodies, PR descriptions, and transcript text stay out of `review.json`. PR comment `body` is copied on purpose. The URL remains the escape hatch for tickets and for opening the comment on the forge.

Transcripts get a gist and no URL. That is the no-leak guarantee, enforced by shape rather than by policy.

A comment with `path` + `side` + `line` is pinned to that line of live git. A comment without a line (PR conversation, not a review comment) stays a source with a quote, not a diff annotation.

Groups get `sources?: string[]` with ids, so a group can name its sources even when the prose does not cite them inline.

### Inline citations

Prose cites a source with standard markdown link syntax and a reserved scheme:

```json
"why": "Reviewers asked for [a cap on retries](source:s2), and [#24](source:s1) tracks the feature."
```

No new syntax. Agents emit markdown links reliably, and the text degrades to readable prose in any renderer. `validate` resolves every `source:` href against `sources` and fails on unknown ids, the same way hunk-ref coverage works. In the UI a stale id renders as plain text and gets flagged, never invented.

Clicking a citation to a line-pinned comment opens the group that holds that hunk, scrolls to the line, and focuses the quote. That is what makes comments first-class. Citations to tickets, transcripts, or unpinned comments keep the hover card.

### UI

Inline citation renders as primary-colored link text with a text-sized kind icon before the first word (icon about 0.8em, kept on the same line as the first word). Hovering shows a card with the kind, label, gist, and the external link. Tried and rejected: superscript icons (illegible at display size) and inline shadcn badges (break the sentence rhythm, read as UI inserted into prose).

Below the What of each group and of the overview, a `SOURCES` row lists all sources for that scope in the existing metadata register (mono label, one-line gist, external-link arrow, no arrow for transcripts). The overview row replaces the current ticket list and keeps the part color dots. No floating panel.

Line-pinned PR comments also render on the live diff, on that line: author, faithful body, link out. Pierre already pins blame onto file lines via `lineAnnotations`; comments should use the same idea on the group diff. Several comments on one line stack. A pointer whose path or line no longer matches live git is flagged like a stale hunk ref. Git wins. The quote is still shown, the pin is marked broken, never replaced.

Show and hide comments on the diffs with a header toggle in the same register as Wrap. Default on when the review has any line-pinned comment. The control is absent when none exist. Keyboard: `c`. Hiding comments does not hide the Sources row or inline citations. Clicking a citation to a pinned comment still opens the line, and shows that quote even if comments are hidden.

Mockups (against the pr32 fixture, gist row and inline marks; comments-on-diff is not in these shots):

![Overview with inline citations and sources row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/matemolnar8/comprehende/assets/sources-mock/mocks/overview-prefix-icon.png)

![Group with inline citations and sources row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/matemolnar8/comprehende/assets/sources-mock/mocks/group-prefix-icon.png)

### Skill

The skill already reads these sources for the why. New work is: assign ids, write labels and gists, emit `sources`, cite inline where the prose leans on a specific source, and for review comments copy author, body, path, side, and line from the forge. Vendor specifics (how to fetch a GitHub review comment vs a Jira ticket) stay at the skill level.

### Out of scope

- Copying ticket bodies, PR descriptions, or transcript text
- Fetching or refreshing source content at serve time
- Any vendor API in the CLI or UI
- Comment threads as a nested tree (flatten or emit one source per comment)

Posted by Cursor [claude-fable-5]",
